steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Addiction is a chronic disorder characterised by compulsive engagement in rewarding stimuli despite harmful consequences. Physical dependence: body needs the substance to function normally (withdrawal symptoms without it). Psychological dependence: emotional/mental need (craving, inability to cope without it).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Biological explanation: the mesolimbic dopamine pathway (reward pathway). Addictive substances and behaviours cause dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens, producing pleasure. Repeated use reduces natural dopamine response, requiring more of the substance to achieve the same effect (tolerance). Genetic vulnerability: inherited differences in dopamine receptor genes.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Learning theory explanation: classical conditioning - environmental cues become associated with the addictive behaviour (e.g. the smell of a pub triggers craving for alcohol). Operant conditioning - positive reinforcement (pleasure from substance) and negative reinforcement (withdrawal relief) maintain addiction.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cognitive explanation: self-medication hypothesis (people use substances to cope with negative emotions). Expectancy theory (beliefs about substance effects influence use). Gamblers fallacy: the mistaken belief that past random events affect future probability (e.g. 'I'm due a win').

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how the dopamine reward pathway contributes to addiction. | Compare biological and learning theory explanations of addiction. | Evaluate treatments for addiction, considering both biological and psychological approaches.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Dopamine reward pathway: substance -> dopamine release -> pleasure -> reinforcement -> addiction. Classical conditioning = CUES trigger craving. Operant conditioning = REINFORCEMENT maintains use. Physical dependence = body needs it. Psychological dependence = mind needs it. Both need treating.
